Ben —

Attached are Hightide’s redlines for the MSA and proposed order form focusing on uptime guarantees and service credit mechanics. Key asks: tighten the uptime target to 99.95% for production-tier, expand the definition of downtime to include degraded KV-cache performance, and shorten the notice period for maintenance from 14 days to 7 days for emergency patches.

We also flagged the credit calculation: they want daily credit accrual (vs. monthly) and a per-incident cap of 20% of monthly fees. Please confirm receipt and whether Redwood can accept these without escalating to Legal / Execs.

Thanks,
Michael Cho
Legal — Hightide Health

Michael / Sara —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. I uploaded the PDF to the shared Drive link. Quick read-through with our AM/Legal: two items look like standard negotiation territory, two will need legal/ops alignment. High level:

- Uptime target: 99.95% for production tier is a material change vs our standard 99.9% for this class of reserved capacity. I need to confirm tradeoffs with capacity and credits.
- Expanded "downtime" to include KV-cache degradation — ops wants to treat performance degradation as an incidents class but with different measurement windows.
- Maintenance notice: shortening to 7 days for emergency patches is reasonable for critical security fixes; we need explicit carveouts for scheduled major upgrades.
- Credit cadence: daily accrual will require changes to billing and finance flows; suggest monthly accrual but with clear per-incident payout triggers.

I'm looping in Laura (legal) and Markus (SRE lead) to propose a compromise we can present back: 99.925% uptime, performance degradation measured by p95 token latency >= X ms for >= 5 continuous minutes, 7-day notice allowed only for CVE-class emergency patches, and monthly credits but with per-incident calculation.

Can you confirm Hightide’s flexibility on the measurement window for performance issues and whether they can live with a per-incident cap based on prorated daily fees? If yes, I'll coordinate a short call next week with Laura and Markus.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: proposed language and fallback positions for Hightide SLA

Team —

Reviewed Michael's redlines overnight. Draft positions below for Ben to present; I recommend we prepare redline text snippets so Legal and Hightide can iterate quickly:

1) Uptime: agree to 99.925% for the Reserved-Prod tier for the initial 12-month term; include an annual review and rebaseline clause tied to average weekly utilization. Proposed text: "Customer Uptime Target: 99.925% measured per calendar month; deviations will be evaluated under the Service Credit table."

2) Performance degradation: define two buckets — "Total Outage" (no requests succeeding) and "Severe Degradation" (p95 latency > 2.5x baseline for >= 5 continuous minutes). Severe Degradation triggers reduced credits (half the outage credit) and requires documented mitigation steps.

3) Maintenance windows: accept 7-day notice for emergency security patches defined as CVE-scored >=7.0; scheduled maintenance remains at 14 days with up to 4 maintenance windows annually for Reserved-Prod.

4) Credits: keep monthly accrual for operational simplicity but allow per-incident invoicing (i.e., finance can issue a one-off credit if incident meets threshold). Cap per-incident at 25% of monthly fees to balance risk.

5) Measurement & reporting: include a mutually accessible status feed (read-only) and a monthly SLA report; incidents > P3 must have RCA within 10 business days.

If these are acceptable to Ops, I can produce redline snippets and loop in Legal counsel for Hightide. If not, suggest we set a 30-minute call Mon/Tue to finalize.

-Laura
Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference

Ben / Laura —

Thanks for the quick internal review and the concrete fallback positions. A couple of clarifications from our side before a call:

- 99.925% is closer to what we can accept (we were pushing for 99.95%). We need confirmation that the baseline re-review can't be used to degrade the target mid-contract. Suggest language: "Any change to the Uptime Target requires mutual written agreement and may only be implemented at renewal."
- Performance degradation bucket: Hightide accepts the two-bucket approach but asks that the threshold (2.5x baseline) be explicitly tied to a rolling 28-day baseline to avoid noise from ramp events.
- Credits cap: prefer 20% per incident but open to 25% if tied to a higher uptime floor (e.g., 99.93% rather than 99.925%).

We can do a 30-minute call Monday 10:00 AM PT to close open items and run through the redline snippets if that works. Please send an invite.

Regards,
Michael Cho

Michael / Sara —

Thanks — call scheduled Mon 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite sent). Summary of what we'll propose on the call and the options table for quick decisioning:

Option A (Redwood preferred):
- Uptime: 99.925% monthly; no unilateral mid-term changes without mutual written agreement.
- Performance: Severe Degradation = p95 >= 2.5x rolling 28-day baseline for >= 5 continuous minutes.
- Maintenance: 7-day notice for CVE>=7 emergency patches; 14 days for other scheduled maintenance.
- Credits: monthly accrual; per-incident payout allowed; cap per incident = 25% of monthly fees.

Option B (Hightide rollback):
- Uptime: 99.93% monthly (closer to Hightide ask) with a 20% per-incident cap and the same performance measurement.

Please have decisionmakers on the call for quick sign-off; Laura will bring redline text and Markus will join to cover measurement and reporting. After call, we'll upload a redline PDF (RW response) and circulate a DocuSign envelope for the amended order form.
